display.tagline: The archive lives; the living forecast dies.
display.certainty_sentence: The failure is usually not that a decision changes. It is that we lose the evidence to know which decision is right.

systems.name: Coastal and beach erosion
systems.central_question: Will the next storm reach the dune, cross it, or flood what's behind it, and how fast is the shoreline moving?
systems.headline: The chain behind a storm-erosion forecast for a barrier island
systems.frame: The United States built a federated coastal observing system across USACE, USGS, and NOAA. Its resilience comes from redundancy in observation; its vulnerability sits at a handful of human and computational convergence points that turn observations into decisions.

scenarios.name: Pull the plug on the airplane
scenarios.lesson: Level 4 arrives not because the old archive disappeared, but because a physical state of the coastline passed through time without being measured.
scenarios.what_broke_first: Nothing anyone noticed. The maps still worked and the forecasts still ran. The first loss was a survey window that closed.

trigger.event: next major hurricane landfall on an unsurveyed coast

timeline.note: No federal pre/post dataset for the reshaped island

record_bar.note: You cannot fly the coastline as it existed five years earlier.

scenarios.name: Pull the plug on the scientists
scenarios.lesson: Existing lidar survives, DSAS survives as software, the papers survive. The human layer between observations and coastal intelligence erodes, and the FY27 budget already describes what that looks like.
scenarios.what_broke_first: Rapid storm response on two of three coastlines, and 27 positions.

timeline.note: Event-dependent: a storm opportunity can be lost immediately
Field response capacity reduced; FY27 Greenbook: one of three coastlines

scenarios.name: Pull the plug on the forecast
scenarios.lesson: The observations still exist, NOAA still predicts waves and surge, USGS still has the morphology. The integrated answer, whether the water reaches the dune toe, crest, or inundates behind it, disappears. Data are not the same thing as information infrastructure.

timeline.note: Six-day forecast disappears after existing horizon expires
Warning issued without erosion and overwash guidance

record_bar.note: The forecast can be restarted; the storms it would have covered are in the past.

systems.name: Coastal flooding and sea level
systems.central_question: Where is the water now, how often are we flooding, and how fast is the baseline changing?
systems.headline: One tide gauge, three clocks
systems.frame: Pull one tide gauge and you start three failure clocks at once. The flood-information clock starts immediately. The flood-climatology clock takes months to years. The climate-record clock takes years to show damage, but the missing observations are irrecoverable from day one.

branches.name: How fast is the baseline changing?

scenarios.name: Pull one long-running tide gauge
scenarios.lesson: You can restart the gauge. You cannot remeasure yesterday's sea.
scenarios.what_broke_first: The local water level stopped being confirmed. The long-term trend box stayed green.

timeline.note: Local water level not confirmed; nearby gauges and models may substitute
Long-term trend essentially unchanged; precision depends on record length (NOAA FAQ)
Multiple tide cycles and possibly flood events pass unobserved

systems.name: Harmful algal blooms
systems.central_question: Is this water, or this seafood, dangerous right now?
systems.headline: We can still see the bloom from space. Can we tell whether it can poison someone?
systems.frame: There is no single U.S. HAB observing system to unplug. NOAA provides satellites, models, and research money; the decisive observations and toxin measurements are made regionally by states, universities, tribes, labs, and volunteers. The inexpensive regional link is what makes the expensive federal forecast actionable.

branches.name: Pacific Northwest: domoic acid and Dungeness crab
Gulf of Maine: the winter survey

scenarios.name: Pull the plug on the toxin sampling
scenarios.lesson: A closure is evidence the warning system worked. The failure state is not that the fishery closes; it is that nobody can tell whether it should be open.
scenarios.what_broke_first: Certainty. The ocean was still there and the satellite still saw the bloom. Without fresh cells and toxin measurements, managers could no longer tell with confidence whether seafood was safe to harvest.

timeline.note: Depends on region; the Gulf forecast is immediate
Increased sampling ordered from remaining capacity
Bloom toxicity and species status uncertain
2015: $97.5M lost crab revenue when the system worked; without sampling, the decision is blind
Long biological record contains permanent gaps

scenarios.name: Pull the cell counts behind the respiratory forecast
scenarios.lesson: A three-hour forecast with 30-hour reach starts aging the day its observations stop.

timeline.note: Forecast refreshes every 3 hours from cell counts; input is stale within days

scenarios.name: Cancel the winter cyst survey
scenarios.lesson: Nothing happens for months. Then spring arrives and the seasonal forecast has no initial condition.

timeline.note: Seasonal forecast cannot be initialized; weekly forecasts do not issue
State managers lose the seasonal risk outlook

scenarios.name: Zero the NCCOS research line
scenarios.lesson: The system does not go dark tomorrow. Existing grants continue. Then one project expires, then another; a technician leaves; an instrument isn't serviced; a regional observation disappears; a forecast loses its input.

systems.name: Weather balloons (NWS upper-air network and IGRA)
systems.central_question: Will there be tornadoes this afternoon, and will the record show what the atmosphere looked like this morning?
systems.headline: One balloon, two irreversibilities
systems.frame: The same 7 a.m. sounding that tells a forecaster whether this afternoon will spawn tornadoes becomes, by evening, a permanent line in a record that began in 1905. Miss the launch and you lose both, on different clocks.

scenarios.name: Pull the plug on the 7 a.m. launch
scenarios.lesson: The program line survived intact; the capability didn't. The balloon went up at noon instead of 7, and on April 13 the watch came 30 minutes before the first tornado.
scenarios.what_broke_first: Pre-dawn staffing. Nothing in the budget changed.

timeline.note: Same-day severe outlook loses its pre-convective profile

trigger.event: next same-day severe outbreak on a morning with missing soundings

timeline.note: April 13, 2026: watch about 30 minutes before first touchdown
ECMWF 2015: degradation local first, downstream within days
Each missed launch is a permanent hole in that station's record from the day it is missed
Warning lead time depends on watch context

record_bar.note: Kansas sites, from public upper-air records cited by Rep. Davids, May 2026.

scenarios.name: Pull 17% of the network
scenarios.lesson: Redundancy at the global scale is not redundancy where the tornadoes are. Hemispheric skill scores barely move, which is what NOAA says; the Plains lose the profiles that matter for convection.

timeline.note: ECMWF 2015 Russia case: errors grow over the region first
Largest in winter when satellite data over land are used less

scenarios.name: Pull the plug on the archive
scenarios.lesson: Every forecast still runs and nobody notices for months. Then the 120-year temperature record stops updating, RATPAC stops, and European reanalyses lose their U.S. source.

timeline.note: Derived products (RATPAC) stop; RHARM loses its source
SEDAC pattern: preservation lapses once staff disperse

systems.name: Ocean heat content
systems.central_question: The ocean stores most of the excess heat in the climate system. How do we know how much, where it went, and how deep it reached?
systems.headline: Three plugs: where, how it crosses the currents, how deep
systems.frame: Argo gives the global repeat field. XBT gives high-resolution repeat sections through the boundary currents. GO-SHIP gives the full-depth, climate-quality reference. Pull one plug and the ocean keeps warming; we stop being able to see one dimension of where the heat went.

branches.name: How heat crosses the fast currents
How far down, and against what reference

scenarios.name: Stop buying U.S. floats
scenarios.lesson: Existing floats don't die when Congress stops buying replacements. The array thins as batteries fail, and the U.S. share of a 26-nation system shrinks.

timeline.note: Regional gaps growing; estimate increasingly model-dependent

scenarios.name: Stop the high-density XBT lines
scenarios.lesson: The global field remains. Boundary-current heat transport loses resolution. The next transect, not the calendar, is the clock.

timeline.note: Two seasonal sections may be missing

scenarios.name: Cancel a GO-SHIP occupation
scenarios.lesson: The instant the ship passes the opportunity window without sampling, that ocean state is gone. You cannot return in 2036 and measure what the abyss and the carbon inventory were in 2026.

timeline.note: Deep and BGC Argo lose a reference

scenarios.name: Pull all three
scenarios.lesson: The archive lives. The ocean keeps changing. We stop measuring the change. History wasn't deleted; we stopped writing the next page.

timeline.note: Estimate increasingly dependent on models and old climatology
Current global ocean heat change no longer adequately observed

exposure.label: Argo observational reach
exposure.basis: About 100,000 profiles a year; 3 million by July 2024; NOAA funds roughly half the international program

exposure.label: XBT niche
exposure.basis: About 15% of non-mooring temperature profiles but about 80% of boundary-current profiles

exposure.label: What depends on OHC
exposure.basis: Earth energy imbalance, steric sea level, climate model validation, hurricane intensity forecasting

leverage.text: No dollar ratio is defensible here. The reach of each observing leg is the measure: global profiles, boundary-current resolution, full-depth reference.

bridge.summary: Concept only until the funding layer is researched: the WOD/OCL harmonization staff at NCEI (the human layer that makes Argo, XBT, and GO-SHIP comparable) and XBT ship-of-opportunity operations are the two legs where a philanthropic bridge is plausible at low single-digit millions; float procurement and GO-SHIP ship time are not.
bridge.vehicle: NCEI cooperative institute partner; AOML SOOP partners
bridge.cannot_do: Buy floats at scale or charter global-class research vessels.
